review.summary: Phase 21's plan-and-provenance chunk delivers what it claims. I independently verified the vendored management 0.86.0 corpus (manifest source + 4 vendorArtifacts + MIT license pin, byte-consistent sha256/gitBlobSha1/bytes across manifest and source.json), the hash chain from the pinned audit inventory to the vendored YAML and normalized JSON, the 7-source/160-operation inventory with full per-operation parameters/body/responses/security/servers/reference closure, the complete 68-delta classification with lossless old/new values and dispositions, and the immutable retention floor with its independent seed, digest-origin proof and additive-only subset semantics. Every substantive design claim in docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md that I could check against actual bytes held: VERTEX_AI/N8N are the only new TargetConnectionType members (MS_COPILOT_STUDIO and CUSTOM_TARGET_ADAPTER already exist in the frozen 0.7.67 baseline), ResponseMode gains REALTIME, AudioFormat carries PCM16, ProfilingStatusFilter is exactly the four claimed values, TargetStatusFilter narrows 7→2 (so the QUEUED/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/PARTIALLY_COMPLETE migration table is accurate), old ProfilingStatus really did contain INIT and QUEUED, the five target response declarations match the vendor schemas, TargetListOptions is #[non_exhaustive] with free-form `status`, and the spec advertises api.sase... while the SDK default stays api.apps... Evidence is real, not prose: the 23 recorded checks in docs/checks/phase-21.json match tools/check_phase.py:135-170 exactly in content and order, all with real invocations and exit_code 0, and the planning-metadata exception is enforced byte-exactly against git baseline bytes with single-occurrence quoted hash replacement. No SDK runtime file changed. Remaining defects are robustness and maintainability, not correctness: the delta classifier fails open on constraint keywords outside its reviewed-digest set, the generated retention artifact is a 27k-line duplicate of the seed whose computed inputs are silently discarded, and the management source.json's semantic fields have no verifier. No blocker or high findings.

findings.description: disposition() claims to "fail closed on unclassified changes" (docstring line 149), but the REVIEWED_SEMANTIC_CHANGES digest requirement only applies when kind == 'changed' AND path[-1] is in {type, format, enum, anyOf, oneOf, $ref}. Two classes of narrowing therefore reach the schema-name classifier and are auto-dispositioned with no reviewed digest: (a) kind == 'added' for a constraint leaf, e.g. ['components','schemas','TargetSchema','properties','name','enum'] added, falls through to line 196 and returns 'new_behavior_and_alias'; (b) kind == 'changed' for constraint keys absent from the set, notably 'additionalProperties', 'default', 'maxLength', 'minLength', 'minimum', 'pattern', 'items', 'const'. A vendor flip of additionalProperties true->false or a changed `default` on an existing property would be silently classified as reviewed new behavior. I confirmed none of the current 68 deltas exercise this (all 'default'/'additionalProperties' occurrences in compatibility-decisions.json sit inside wholly added/removed schema values), so current output is correct, but this is the classifier that phase 25 drift detection and the next upstream re-pin inherit, and defaults/open-object acceptance are behavior-critical in this codebase.
findings.required_fix: Apply the reviewed-digest requirement to any delta whose leaf key is a schema constraint keyword regardless of kind, and extend the keyword set to at least additionalProperties, default, const, pattern, maxLength, minLength, maximum, minimum, maxItems, minItems and items. Add regressions to tools/test_red_team_management.py covering an added `enum` on an existing property and a changed `default`/`additionalProperties` leaf, asserting 'Unclassified'.

findings.description: retained_floor() returns {**floor, 'seed', 'seedSha256', 'preservationCheck'}, so contracts/airs-retained-capabilities.json is the immutable seed plus three keys. I confirmed this by comparing top-level keys and content of contracts/airs-retained-capabilities.json and contracts/compatibility/airs-0.2.2-retention.json: identical 27,2xx-line bodies, differing only by preservationCheck/seed/seedSha256. Consequences: (1) the repository carries two near-identical ~27k-line artifacts; (2) every value computed at lines 382-393 ('policy', 'preservedPolicies', 'evidenceLimit', 'baselineCommit', 'schemaVersion', and the freshly extracted exports/methods/defaultBindings) is discarded for output purposes and exists only as the comparison operand, which is not evident from the code; (3) test_retention_includes_all_baseline_methods_exports_defaults (3820/448/23/14) asserts seed numbers rather than current-ledger numbers, and `--check` byte comparison of the generated file can never detect ledger additions. The plan's description of the artifact as an inventory of "3820 frozen export mappings, 448 native methods…" reads as current state when it is a floor copy.
findings.required_fix: Either stop emitting the duplicate (keep contracts/compatibility/airs-0.2.2-retention.json as the single floor and have the tool emit only a small provenance/verification receipt), or emit the actual current inventory with the floor recorded by reference. Rename the local variable at line 382 (for example `current_inventory`) and comment that it is a comparison operand, and assert the 3820/448/23/14 counts against the freshly extracted ledgers rather than the floor copy.

findings.description: The management corpus ships a source.json recording expectedOperations 42, openapiVersion 3.1.0, apiVersion 0.86.0, sha256/bytes/gitBlobSha1, licensePath/licenseSha256/licenseSpdx and the js-yaml 4.3.2 pin, but no tool reads it. I grepped tools/ for red-team-management, expectedOperations and openapiVersion: only tools/red_team_dataplane.py:79 and tools/test_red_team_dataplane.py:18 consume an expectedOperations pin, and those are the 0.93.0 data-plane corpus. red_team_management.py derives everything from contracts/manifest.json plus the pinned audit inventory and never asserts spec['openapi'] == '3.1.0' (red_team_dataplane.load():75 does). verify-contracts.py only tracks the file's bytes and cross-checks repository/commit/license against the manifest source, not the file's internal fields. The values are currently consistent with the manifest, so this is latent, not an active defect, but it is an inconsistent pattern: a reader reasonably assumes source.json is the authority it is for the data plane.
findings.required_fix: In red_team_management.build(), load VENDOR/'source.json' and assert its path, sha256, bytes, licensePath/licenseSha256, openapiVersion, apiVersion and expectedOperations against the actual YAML bytes, the license file, spec['openapi'], spec['info']['version'] and the operation count, mirroring red_team_dataplane.load():64-80, with a test that each mismatch raises.

findings.description: impl_contains() strips raw strings (203), normal strings (204) and char literals (205) before stripping comments (206). A line comment containing an unpaired double quote, for example `// don"t`, is therefore tokenized as the start of a string literal and the following source up to the next quote is blanked, which can make a genuinely present inherent method invisible (false 'Missing Rust function') or, in the mirror case, let a non-top-level fn appear balanced. The existing test only covers a string containing a brace (line 111). Static native-binding verification is the weakest link in the "all 160 operations are mapped" claim, so its tokenizer ordering matters even though no current source file triggers it.
findings.required_fix: Strip comments before strings (or tokenize line/block comments and strings in a single pass), and add a regression in tools/test_red_team_management.py using a source whose line comment contains an unbalanced double quote and whose impl genuinely defines the method.

findings.description: REVIEWED_SEMANTIC_CHANGES binds 17 reviewed semantic changes to sha256(encoded(identity)) digests, which is a good tamper binding, but there is no documented or tooled way to produce those digests at the next upstream re-pin. The failure message 'Unclassified semantic value change: {path}' tells a maintainer nothing about the required artifact, and neither docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md nor the module docstring describes the procedure. Phase 25 explicitly re-pins a new pan.dev tree, so this will be hit.
findings.required_fix: Document the digest-construction procedure (identity = the path/kind/old/new subset, encoded() canonical form) in the module docstring and in the plan's source-authority section, and have the error path state that a maintainer must review the printed old/new values and register the computed digest, so the step is reproducible without reading the implementation.

findings.description: NOTICE names only the Red Team data-plane pan.dev revision afef9d08030a56e18a04ea078f589313f1fa2b0c / 0.93.0 for derived material, relying on the general line 7 pointer to contracts/manifest.json for everything else. The new redistributed management source (pan.dev 582e30543bf2, license pan-dev-582e30543bf2) is correctly registered in the manifest and licenses, and NOTICE is deliberately frozen for phase 21, so nothing is wrong today. However docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:69 says only "Preserve MIT license and notices" and neither it nor the phase 22/24 milestone lists schedules extending NOTICE once management-derived models enter the SDK and the published archive.
findings.required_fix: Add an explicit phase 22 or phase 24 item to docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md requiring NOTICE to name the management 0.86.0 pan.dev revision alongside the data-plane revision before publication, in the same qualified source change that lands the derived models.

evidence: docs/checks/phase-21.json is byte-identical in content to the supplied docs/reviews/phase-21-chunk-plan-and-provenance-attempt-03.checks.json (same checked_at 2026-10-19T13:00:35.930783+00:00, same 23 entries); all 23 have real `invocation` arrays with resolved interpreter paths and exit_code 0, timeout false. No entry is synthetic, skipped or placeholder.

The 23 recorded checks match tools/check_phase.py:135-170 management_commands(21) exactly in membership and order: 3 phase-21 freeze/provenance commands, then the 10 common commands (2 git diff --check with the vendor-YAML exclusion, 3 verify-contracts modes, red_team_management --check --verify-retention-origin, 3 unittest suites, private-material receipt check), then test_ci.py, 3 generator --check tools, verify_native_fixtures --require-test-bindings, red_team_dataplane --check --require-complete, schema-oracle, verify-gateway-specimens, generate_validation, generate_models.

tools/verify-contracts.py --self-test stdout records 27 rejected tampering cases including the new vendor-ownership set: unowned-vendor-file, missing-vendor-file, modified-vendor-file, vendor-license-commit, duplicate-source-id, vendor-artifact-origin, vendor-artifact-omission, vendor-artifact-escape, vendor-symlink, unowned-vendor-version.

tools/verify-contracts.py:29 scopes VENDOR_ROOTS to contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0 only; lines 471-478 sweep the parent directory and reject any file outside a registered version, and lines 479-489 require exact corpus/manifest file-set equality. The data-plane and Portkey vendor trees are not absorbed, matching the plan's ownership rule.

Provenance chain verified by reading: tools/red_team_management.py:27 pins inventory.json sha256; docs/research/.../inventory.json:44-54 records upstream sha256 5fbb533b… for the management spec with activeBytesEqualUpstream false; red_team_management.py:319-320 checks the vendored contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/mp-openapi.yaml against that hash; lines 341-345 require the normalized openapi.json to parse equal to the YAML; contracts/manifest.json:1949-1963 and source.json:13-15 record the same sha256 5fbb533b…, gitBlobSha1 9959caca… and 212515 bytes.

tools/check_phase.py:79-132 enforces the planning-metadata exception byte-exactly: require_only_hash_replacements requires each replacement to be a 64-hex value, appear exactly once as a quoted token in the git baseline bytes, and the result to equal the current bytes verbatim; verify_planning_fixture then rehashes the actual corpus file and contracts/manifest.json, and verify_planning_gateway_proof allows exactly the two allowlisted input hashes.

Plan claims checked against vendor bytes: contracts/vendor/.../openapi.json:6592-6611 (TargetConnectionType gains only VERTEX_AI and N8N; frozen mp-openapi.yaml:4470-4471 already contains MS_COPILOT_STUDIO and CUSTOM_TARGET_ADAPTER), :5489-5500 (ResponseMode gains REALTIME), :2605-2611 (AudioFormat includes PCM16), :5300-5310 (ProfilingStatusFilter exactly NOT_STARTED/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED), :9054-9062 (TargetStatusFilter narrowed to DRAFT/ACTIVE from the frozen 7 values at mp-openapi.yaml:5881-5890), frozen mp-openapi.yaml:3559-3569 (old ProfilingStatus did contain INIT and QUEUED, validating the plan's migration table rows).

Endpoint discrepancy verified: contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/mp-openapi.yaml:14-17 advertises https://api.sase.paloaltonetworks.com/ai-red-teaming/mgmt-plane with global bearerAuth, while crates/scm-sdk/src/constants.rs:634-635 retains https://api.apps.paloaltonetworks.com/ai-red-teaming/mgmt-plane; contracts/airs-operations.json:66-70 records the same api.sase /aims/data server for Model Security. The plan's decision to keep current defaults under destination admission is therefore grounded and conservative.

Compatibility-decision completeness: contracts/vendor/.../compatibility-decisions.json contains 68 deltas and 68 category/decision pairs with no unclassified rows; 8 three-element removals all carry component_removed_or_renamed plus a successorReference that exists in the new schema set (COMPONENT_SUCCESSORS covers exactly the 4 *ConnectionParamsBase names x -Input/-Output); rows record lossless old/new plus affectedOperations resolved through both old and new reference closures (e.g. lines 6-31, 33-51).

Retention floor independence verified: tools/red_team_management.py:267-291 loads the floor only from the hash-pinned contracts/compatibility/airs-0.2.2-retention.json, rejects duplicate baselineIds, uses an additive-only `contains` subset, and verify_retention_origin (294-301) rehashes all six RETENTION_LEDGER_PATHS; tools/test_red_team_management.py:163-198 proves removals, emptied rustPaths, a changed default and seed tampering are all rejected while additions are permitted and never rewrite the floor.

scripts/check-private-material.py:135-211 shows --check is a receipt-freshness check that recomputes the git-visible source fingerprint and published-candidate fingerprint and rejects a mismatch, so the recorded {"receiptFresh": true, "privateScanReexecuted": false, "gitVisibleFilesChecked": 1880} binds the earlier scan to the current source rather than merely asserting it.

Phase gating fails closed: tools/red_team_management.py:411-412 rejects --require-through-phase 22-25, and tools/test_red_team_management.py:199-203 executes the CLI for phases 22-25 as a subprocess and asserts nonzero exit with 'static plan evidence cannot advance'.

No SDK runtime change: the recorded git diff against 0a213fe79c7f0c5758f05f53d04a5c577a4f3f4e over crates/scm-sdk, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, LICENSE, NOTICE and the six frozen ledgers exits 0 (only the allowlisted model-regressions fixture is excluded and separately byte-gated), and the git ls-files --others assertion confirms no untracked SDK file was staged for the plan phase.

Model Security class attribution at red_team_management.py:241-244 is a method-name heuristic, but I confirmed it is self-checking: crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/model_security/inventory.rs defines disjoint method sets (ModelSecurityModelsClient list_models/get_model/list_model_versions…, ModelSecurityRulesClient list/list_all/get/list_versions), so any misattribution would fail impl_contains rather than pass silently.

tools/red_team_dataplane.py:59-61 (reused by the management tool) pins js-yaml 4.3.2 and throws 'Unreviewed parser' on any other version, supporting the plan's reproducibility claim; the only secret-shaped strings in the vendored corpus are upstream placeholders ("Bearer sk-xxxxxxxxxxxx" at openapi.json:4373,4399 and mp-openapi.yaml:2955,2971).
limitations: Read-only Read/Glob/Grep only, no shell: I could not recompute the reviewed source fingerprint e2a407ab7c6f413a9b6651011e00c4b9f765dee0761f0e29b2710eee9d308694, re-execute any of the 23 checks, or recompute file sha256 values. I verified evidence by reading the recorded invocations, exit codes and stdout and by independently cross-reading the artifacts those commands assert over, and by confirming the recorded command list matches tools/check_phase.py byte-for-byte in content and order.

docs/checks/phase-21.json is staged-and-modified (AM) in the snapshot git status; I read the working-tree copy and found it consistent with the supplied attempt-03 checks evidence, but I could not diff index against worktree.

The phase-governance chunk artifacts (.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml, tools/review_phase.py, tools/test_management_phases.py, docs/CI.md, docs/RELEASE.md) are outside this chunk's scope; I inspected tools/check_phase.py only where it owns this chunk's artifacts (the phase-21 command list and the planning-fixture/gateway-specimen gates) and otherwise relied on the passing recorded suites.

Static evidence only, as the artifacts themselves state: native-binding verification proves a named inherent method exists, not request construction, wire acceptance or tenant permissions. Phase 22-25 runtime behavior, the five response-declaration fixtures, old-consumer source compatibility and live acceptance are not assessable here and were not judged.

I did not read any credential or tenant-registration material and did not leave the repository; .local/typescript was only referenced as the recorded baseline argument of verify-contracts.py, not inspected.

Finding 1 is a reachability argument from reading disposition() plus a grep over the 68 recorded deltas; I could not execute the function to demonstrate the fail-open path, so the conclusion that it is currently unexercised rests on that grep.
